title: ForgeSight scope review
raw_text:
ForgeSight scope review — 21 August 2026, 15:00
Present: Marcus (Head of Product), Priya (Eng Lead), Wei (Design), Tom (Sales), Dana (Customer Success).

Marcus (Head of Product): This is the scope conversation, not the design conversation. I want to come out of the hour with a pilot we can actually build.
Dana (Customer Success): Then can I start with onboarding, because it's the thing that loses us the first week. A new customer signs in and sees an empty grid. They have no idea what to build.
Marcus (Head of Product): So we ship templates.
Dana (Customer Success): ForgeSight should ship prebuilt dashboard templates per industry, so a new customer sees their own data on day one instead of an empty grid. Retail one, logistics one. Two would do.
Wei (Design): And the other half of that, which is cheaper: a user can duplicate an existing dashboard and edit the copy. Most people don't want to start from nothing, they want to start from what their colleague made.
Marcus (Head of Product): Both in. They're small.
Priya (Eng Lead): The templates are not small, but go on.
Tom (Sales): Right, mine. Trials. I have eleven prospects who will not sign anything until they have clicked around in it themselves. I need a prospect to be able to create a login with an email address and be inside ForgeSight in two minutes.
Priya (Eng Lead): We agreed the opposite of that a week ago. We authenticate through the customer's SAML provider and we store no passwords. A self-serve email login is a second authentication path and a second thing to get breached.
Tom (Sales): Then I can't run a trial.
Priya (Eng Lead): Then we can't say we don't store credentials, which is the sentence that gets us through Meridian's security review.
Tom (Sales): Meridian's already a customer. I'm talking about the eleven who aren't.
Priya (Eng Lead): And I'm talking about the one breach that ends the pilot. These are not the same risk.
Marcus (Head of Product): I'm not settling that in this meeting. Both of you write it up.
Tom (Sales): It's blocking eleven deals.
Priya (Eng Lead): It's unresolved, is what it is.
Marcus (Head of Product): Next. Alerts. Dana, you had a number.
Dana (Customer Success): Yes. If we're going to do threshold alerts at all, they have to be fast enough to act on. An alert email has to arrive within five minutes of the threshold being crossed. Halcyon's whole use case is a stockout, and a stockout you learn about an hour later is a report, not an alert.
Priya (Eng Lead): Five minutes I can do. Five minutes on hourly-refreshed data is a slightly odd sentence, but I can do the five minutes.
Marcus (Head of Product): Note the oddness and move on. Security housekeeping — Priya.
Priya (Eng Lead): Short one. No third-party analytics or tracking scripts may run in the customer-facing app. No product analytics vendor, no session recorder, nothing that ships a customer's data to a fourth party.
Tom (Sales): Not even to see what people click?
Priya (Eng Lead): Not in the pilot. Meridian's contract has a subprocessor clause and every one of those tools is a subprocessor.
Marcus (Head of Product): Fine. Now the one I know Wei will not like. I want to cut the tablet view from the pilot. It's a whole second layout, it's Wei's whole week, and every buyer we've actually spoken to demoed on a laptop.
Wei (Design): That's fair, and you know the pipeline better than I do. Though I'd have thought the shift supervisors were the ones who'd be looking at it hourly, and they're the population that doesn't have a laptop. But if the buyers are on laptops, the buyers are on laptops.
Marcus (Head of Product): So you're okay with cutting it.
Wei (Design): I'm okay with you deciding it. I'd want it back in the release after, and I'd want someone to tell Northwind before their supervisors find out by opening it.
Marcus (Head of Product): Noted. Let's call it cut for now.
Dana (Customer Success): Last one from me and it's an operations thing. An admin should be able to see which dashboards have not been opened in the last thirty days. Half of what we build for these people is never looked at and I would like to be able to prove it.
Marcus (Head of Product): That I like. In. And the last constraint, from me, and it isn't negotiable: the pilot runs with three customer accounts only, Northwind, Meridian and Halcyon. Nobody adds a fourth without me.
Tom (Sales): Even if the fourth one signs.
Marcus (Head of Product): Even then.
